methods: The acute screen used 43 acute MEA outputs, the existing vehicle standardization, the original five chemical folds, and five chemical-seeded contexts of three measured concentrations. AnchorBoost was refitted with its frozen 600-iteration recipe. The published conditional neural process (commit f9848800dfab66a8bc005e6b3087153eeaabe9ac) retained its source bytes and used the Gaussian interpolated configuration selected in published NFA folds 1–4, with the output dimension adapted to the screen. Three final-checkpoint models used seeds 0, 1 and 2, 4,000 steps each and batch size 32; their predicted means were averaged. No external test outcomes selected a configuration or checkpoint. MAE was averaged across observed concentration-level means, designs and chemical identities in that order. Paired percentile intervals used 10,000 chemical-identity resamples, seed 0. Both 95% and 97.5% intervals are supplied for the two-screen comparison. Method footnote: Two source IDs represent one chemical identity and occur in the same original fold; their errors are averaged before resampling.
results: AnchorBoost yielded 1.01% lower MAE than the conditional neural process (1.554265 versus 1.570140; K−C -0.015875, 95% interval [-0.030804, -0.001256], 97.5% interval [-0.032964, +0.000778]; n=383 chemical identities). Chemical wins/losses/ties were 209/174/0; fold wins/losses/ties were 5/0/0.
